name: Choose a landing-page build method and keep it speed-safe
what: Decides how a new landing page or funnel page gets built: native theme Liquid section, an AI page-builder app (PageFly, GemPages, Replo, Shogun, Instant, Fudge), or a headless page. The decision is driven by the page's speed budget and the team's coding skill, not by which builder is trendiest, because every page-builder app renders through its own JavaScript layer that adds weight a native section does not carry.
encompasses: list the JS and CSS weight each candidate builder app adds to a page, measured on the brand's own speed profile
compare native Liquid/CSS output (Instant, Fudge-style AI Liquid generation) against proprietary-runtime builders (PageFly, GemPages, Replo, Shogun)
weigh built-in features that avoid extra apps: A/B testing (Replo, GemPages), page-level revenue analytics (Replo, Shogun), personalization by segment (Shogun Smart Pages)
check template count and AI image-to-layout conversion (GemPages GemAI) against the team's actual need for speed of authoring
flag when a page already built in a heavy builder is the diagnosed cause of a speed regression and needs migration to native code
write the migration brief for moving one flagged page off a builder app to native theme code without losing its layout or conversion elements
recommend against buying a new builder app when the theme's own section library already covers the need
trigger: new landing page requested, or a page-builder app named as a speed-audit root cause

name: Set up git-based theme version control and a CI deploy pipeline
what: Replaces duplicate-theme-in-admin editing with a real engineering workflow: theme code in git, Shopify CLI for local development, theme-check linting on every commit, a staging theme that auto-deploys from a branch, and a reviewed merge to the live theme, so changes are reviewable and reversible by commit instead of by remembering which duplicate is which.
encompasses: connect the theme repo to GitHub and configure Shopify's GitHub integration or CLI-based push per environment
run theme-check linting automatically on every commit and block a merge on hard errors
stand up a staging theme URL that mirrors production for every pull request
require a second reviewer or the founder gate before merging to the live theme, matching the existing AI build-agent guardrail
keep a rollback path: one command to redeploy the previous commit's theme package
tag each deploy with the change brief it shipped, so the registry can trace a live change back to its approved idea
migrate an existing admin-duplicated theme history into a single git history without losing the working live version
trigger: store setup, or after a near-miss where a live edit could not be traced or reverted

external_write.surface: store theme (staging first, production on approval)

name: Build and maintain custom app integrations and webhooks
what: Connects the store to systems no off-the-shelf app covers cleanly: an ERP, a warehouse system, a loyalty ledger, a marketplace feed or a regional courier, through the platform's API or a custom app, with auth tokens stored safely, retry logic on failed webhooks and an alert when a sync silently stops.
encompasses: map the fields that must sync both ways (inventory, order status, tracking number, loyalty points) before writing any code
build the custom app or Shopify Flow automation and register the needed webhooks
store API keys and tokens only in the platform's secure app settings or the environment's secret store, never in theme code or a public repo
add retry-with-backoff on failed webhook deliveries and a dead-letter log for ones that never succeed
alert a human when a sync gap is detected (order count mismatch, stale inventory timestamp) rather than fail silently
document the integration's data contract so a future developer does not have to reverse-engineer it
test the integration against a staging or sandbox account of the external system before pointing it at production
trigger: a manual double-entry process is found during a setup or hygiene audit

name: Run continuous automated regression testing on every theme or app change
what: Runs an AI-driven test suite before and after every theme or app change ships: visual diffs across breakpoints, scripted end-to-end flows for browse, cart, discount code and checkout, and self-healing test repair so a small DOM change does not break the whole suite. On failure it produces a video replay, network trace and a written bug report instead of a bare pass or fail.
encompasses: map the store's critical paths into test cases: home, PDP, collection filter, cart, discount code, checkout to confirmation, account login
let an AI mapping step auto-discover new or changed flows after a release instead of hand-writing every test
run visual diffs across mobile, tablet and desktop breakpoints and classify each diff as likely-noise or likely-real before a human reviews it
run the suite in parallel isolated environments so a full pass finishes in minutes, not hours
self-heal a test whose selector changed for a cosmetic reason, and flag ones that fail for a real reason
capture video replay, console errors and network trace on any failure and write a bug report a developer can act on without re-running it
gate a theme deploy on the suite passing, wired into the CI pipeline
test payment and OTP steps with sandboxed credentials, never real customer payment data
trigger: every theme or app deploy, and on a nightly schedule

name: Run real-time uptime and transaction monitoring with alert routing
what: Runs synthetic checks every few minutes against the home page, a key PDP, cart, checkout and on-site search from several regions, plus a real-user page-load feed, and routes an alert to a human the moment any of them degrades or fails, including SSL certificate expiry, instead of waiting for a scheduled housekeeping pass to notice.
encompasses: set up synthetic checks on home, PDP, collection, cart, checkout and search at a chosen interval from more than one region
add a full transaction check that walks add-to-cart through order confirmation on a schedule, not just a page-200 check
track SSL certificate expiry and DNS resolution separately from page uptime
pull real-user monitoring (RUM) page-load data to catch slow-but-not-down degradation synthetic checks miss
route the alert to the right person with an escalation path if the first alert is not acknowledged
keep an incident log with time to detect and time to fix, feeding the post-launch hygiene review
exclude expected maintenance windows from triggering false alerts
trigger: store setup completion, or after any unnoticed outage found in a hygiene review

name: Simulate AI shopper personas through the storefront before shipping a redesign
what: Runs synthetic shopper personas with different intents and devices through the storefront in a sandbox before real traffic sees a redesign, reporting add-to-cart rate, navigation path and where each persona got stuck, and compares two designs head to head so the founder sees a predicted difference before committing real ad spend to a test.
encompasses: define 3 to 6 personas matching the brand's real customer segments (first-time, repeat, price-sensitive, gift buyer)
run each persona through the current site and a candidate redesign in a private, non-indexed sandbox
record add-to-cart rate, click path length and the exact step each persona abandoned at
flag usability friction a persona hit that a human reviewer would likely also hit
compare two theme or page versions side by side on the same personas before an A/B test spends real traffic
state plainly that this is a prediction, not a measured result, and should not replace a real test on a decision with real money at stake
trigger: before a redesign goes to a real A/B test, when the change is expensive to build

name: Configure checkout payment methods and address validation
what: Sets up Shop Pay, PayPal, Apple Pay and a BNPL option (Affirm, Klarna or Afterpay) at checkout, validates the shipping address against USPS before the order is placed, and layers fraud signals onto risky orders, each measured against the brand's own failed-delivery and chargeback rate. Where the brand sells COD in India, adds the market option of a PIN code serviceability check on the PDP, OTP verification and a visible fee on high-value cash-on-delivery orders, and a WhatsApp order-confirmation trigger to cut return-to-origin (RTO); this option reads null for a US brand.
encompasses: enable Shop Pay, PayPal, Apple Pay and a BNPL option (Affirm, Klarna or Afterpay) at checkout
validate the shipping address against USPS before the order is placed, catching a bad ZIP code or an undeliverable address before it ships
screen orders for fraud signals (mismatched billing and shipping, high-risk card BIN, order velocity) and route flagged orders for manual review
show accepted payment badges and a clear BNPL installment estimate near the buy box
trigger an automated order-confirmation message by SMS (with TCPA consent and quiet-hours rules) or email after checkout, with an auto-cancel rule if unconfirmed within a set window
replace the generic carrier tracking link with a branded tracking page that also carries post-purchase upsell content

pass a buyer risk score (first order, high order value, prior chargeback or return-to-sender history) to the fulfilment system so it can flag for manual check, without the site itself running carrier-side exception handling
build a failed-delivery and chargeback analytics view by carrier, ZIP code, product and payment method so the founder can see which lever is moving the number
India market option, reads null for US: show real-time PIN code serviceability on the PDP using the courier or aggregator's API before the shopper adds to cart
India market option, reads null for US: add address auto-fill and phone OTP verification at checkout for COD orders above a set value
India market option, reads null for US: add a visible COD handling fee as a checkout line item, sized to filter impulse orders without losing genuine buyers
India market option, reads null for US: surface a prepaid discount or free-shipping incentive at the exact checkout step where COD is selected
India market option, reads null for US: trigger a WhatsApp order-confirmation message after COD checkout, with an auto-cancel rule if unconfirmed within a set window
India market option, reads null for US: add the brand's RTO rate by PIN code and payment method to the analytics view
inputs: brand's historical chargeback and failed-delivery data
India market option, null for US: courier serviceability API
India market option, null for US: WhatsApp business API access
outputs: India market option, null for US: checkout OTP flow
India market option, null for US: COD fee config
India market option, null for US: WhatsApp confirmation flow
trigger: checkout payment mix, failed-delivery rate or chargeback rate identified as a bottleneck in the metric contract; India market option: COD share and RTO rate identified as a bottleneck

external_write.surface: store checkout settings; India market option: WhatsApp business account

human_role: e-commerce web manager, payments specialist; India market option: RTO-reduction freelancer

name: Track platform release notes and plan feature adoption or migration
what: Reads each platform release (Shopify Editions twice a year, WooCommerce and WordPress core updates, an installed app's deprecation notice, an API version sunset date) and turns it into two short lists for the founder: native features that can now retire a paid app, and breaking changes that need a fix before the sunset date, so the store never gets caught by a deprecation it did not see coming.
encompasses: read each Shopify Editions release and the platform's API version deprecation calendar on its schedule
match new native features against the brand's current paid app list to flag a possible app to retire
flag any announced breaking change against code the store actually uses, not a generic checklist
set a reminder ahead of every API version sunset date the store depends on
write a short adopt-or-ignore recommendation per release, not a full changelog dump
check WooCommerce or custom-platform framework updates the same way when that is the brand's platform
inputs: current app and API version list
trigger: a platform release lands, or a deprecation notice arrives

name: Maintain a site-wide design system and component library
what: Documents the brand's spacing, color, typography and button tokens once, then checks every new theme section and page-builder page against them, so a landing page built in a page-builder app does not drift from the native theme's look, and hands a developer or builder a spec instead of a screenshot to match by eye.
encompasses: document color, spacing, typography and component tokens from the current live theme
check every new homepage or PDP section, whether built natively or in a page-builder app, against the token set before it ships
flag drift: a button radius, font size or color that does not match the documented token
produce a Figma-to-Liquid or Figma-to-builder handoff spec for a new section so a developer does not guess spacing from a picture
keep one canonical component list so the same 'FAQ block' or 'comparison table' is not rebuilt slightly differently five times
trigger: a new page or section is briefed, or a drift is spotted in QA

name: Maintain a staging environment that mirrors production data and theme
what: Keeps a staging copy of the store, theme and a recent product and price snapshot in sync with production, so a change, an app trial or a migration can be tested against real-looking data before it ever reaches a live customer, separate from the CI pipeline's code-only staging theme.
encompasses: stand up a staging store or sandboxed duplicate on the same platform
refresh its product, price and inventory snapshot from production on a schedule, never the reverse
mirror the live theme and installed app list into staging before a risky change
password-protect the staging store and keep it out of search indexes
tear down or reset staging data on request so it never becomes a second source of truth
use staging, not production, for every app trial and every AI build-agent session
trigger: store setup, or before any change flagged as risky

name: Build no-code automation rules for site-side operational triggers
what: Uses the platform's own automation layer (Shopify Flow or equivalent) to wire small operational rules directly into the store instead of a developer hand-coding each one: auto-tag a high-risk order for manual review, auto-hold an order from a customer with a chargeback or return-to-sender history (a COD RTO offender in India), auto-apply gift wrap above a cart value, auto-alert the founder on a stockout of a top SKU on its own PDP.
encompasses: list the recurring manual actions a store manager currently does by hand that are pure if-this-then-that logic
build each rule in the platform's native automation tool so it needs no custom app and no hosting
test each rule against a real historical order before turning it on live
log every automated action it takes so a human can audit what fired and why
avoid stacking automation rules that touch the same object in a conflicting order
route anything that needs judgment, not just if-then logic, to a human queue instead of automating it
trigger: a repetitive manual task is found in a hygiene or ops audit

name: Set up a self-serve returns and exchange portal on-site
what: Configures a customer-facing returns and exchange flow on the store (a dedicated app or a native flow), with exchange-for-store-credit incentives sized against real margin, so a return does not always mean a lost sale, and hands the fulfilment-side restocking rule to ops rather than building it itself.
encompasses: select and configure a returns app or native flow against the brand's actual return window and condition rules
set an exchange-for-store-credit incentive with a real bonus amount the margin can support
surface return reasons in a structured way so the data feeds product and copy fixes elsewhere
keep the return portal's copy consistent with the published returns policy page word for word
hand the restocking and refund-timing rule to the operations specialist instead of building warehouse logic here
test the full return-request-to-resolution flow as a real customer would
trigger: a high return or exchange volume is found in hygiene monitoring

name: Support agentic checkout for third-party AI shopping assistants
what: Makes the store's product data, pricing and checkout machine-readable enough for a third-party AI shopping assistant acting on a shopper's behalf to find a product and complete a purchase, then tests that path end to end, since this channel is new and unproven but growing.
encompasses: verify the product feed and structured data an outside AI agent would read (price, stock, variant, shipping cost) are accurate and current
check the checkout can complete a purchase from an agent-initiated session without a broken step a human would silently work around
confirm order attribution correctly tags an agent-initiated purchase so it does not get miscounted as organic or paid
flag any step (a CAPTCHA, a mandatory account creation) that blocks an agent from completing a purchase, and decide with the founder whether to relax it
keep this channel read-only in measurement until the founder has seen at least a handful of real agent-driven orders
trigger: agent-driven orders start appearing in order source data, or the founder asks about this channel

name: Auto-sequence PDP images from the brand's own click-map and zoom data
what: A capability no tool sells yet: instead of a human guessing a better product-image order and running a slow A/B test, the agent reads which images shoppers actually zoom into, skip past or abandon on, and proposes a re-sequenced gallery ranked by real attention data, with the reasoning shown so the founder can approve before it ships.
encompasses: pull per-image zoom, dwell and skip events from the site's own click-map or session-replay data, never a generic benchmark
rank the existing image set by which ones hold attention longest before a scroll-away or an add-to-cart
propose a re-sequenced gallery order with the reasoning per swap, not just a new order with no explanation
flag when there is not yet enough session volume on a SKU to trust the ranking, and say so instead of guessing
size this as a proposal for the founder gate, not an automatic live change, since it touches a live PDP
inputs: click-map or session-replay data per PDP
trigger: a PDP has enough session volume and an unresolved add-to-cart drop-off

name: Cap exit-intent and cart-abandonment discounts to a margin-safe ceiling in real time
what: A capability no tool sells yet: an exit-intent popup or an abandoned-cart discount is normally a single flat number set once by a human. Here the agent computes, in code, the maximum discount that specific cart can take and still clear the brand's real per-order margin floor, using landed cost and shipping cost already in the brand record, so the offer flexes by cart instead of guessing one number for every visitor.
encompasses: read landed cost, shipping cost and any active promo already applied for the exact cart at the moment of exit intent
compute the maximum discount in code that still clears the founder's set margin floor for that order
never let the model estimate the number; the ceiling is arithmetic from the brand's own cost data
show the founder the ceiling logic before turning the offer live, and cap it below the computed ceiling if the founder wants a buffer
fall back to no discount, not a guessed discount, when a cost input for that SKU is missing
trigger: exit-intent or cart-abandonment offer is being designed or already underperforming

name: Build an on-site visual product search from an uploaded photo
what: A capability no tool sells yet at the brand's scale: a shopper uploads or snaps a photo (a style they saw elsewhere, or a product they already own) and the site returns the closest real SKUs by visual similarity, using an image embedding model matched against the brand's own product photos, kept separate from any competitor-image use since only the shopper's own photo is compared, never stored as a competitor asset.
encompasses: embed every live product's real photos once and keep the index current as the catalogue changes
accept a shopper-uploaded photo, embed it the same way, and return the nearest real SKUs, never a generated or redrawn product
cap the feature to product discovery only; never claim a visual match is exact
fall back cleanly to text search when no close visual match exists
keep uploaded shopper photos private and short-lived, never stored as training or competitor data
trigger: on-site search bottleneck diagnosed and the catalogue is visually distinct enough to benefit

name: Add a click-to-WhatsApp catalog and buy flow on the PDP
what: Adds a pre-purchase WhatsApp channel for markets where WhatsApp commerce is common (India, EU, LATAM): a click-to-WhatsApp button on the PDP that opens a chat pre-filled with the exact SKU and variant, backed by the brand's WhatsApp catalog, for shoppers who trust a chat conversation with a human or a bot more than a cart, and routes the resulting cart-recovery and support load to the lifecycle specialist rather than handling it here. Reads null and does not run for a US-default brand.
encompasses: sync the live product catalogue (price, stock, variant) to the brand's WhatsApp Business catalog on a schedule
add a click-to-WhatsApp button on the PDP that pre-fills the exact SKU, variant and a template question
confirm the button only appears in a market where WhatsApp commerce is legal and commonly used (India, EU, LATAM), never for a US-default brand
measure how many PDP-to-WhatsApp clicks convert to an order, separate from normal add-to-cart, so it is not double-counted
hand the WhatsApp conversation flow itself, cart recovery and support scripting to the lifecycle specialist
trigger: COD or trust-driven checkout hesitation diagnosed as a bottleneck in a WhatsApp-commerce market (India, EU, LATAM); reads null for US

external_write.surface: store PDP template, WhatsApp Business catalog

name: Configure consent-based tag gating for CCPA, CPRA and other state privacy laws
what: Builds a cookie and tag consent layer that actually gates tracking scripts by the visitor's region and choice, rather than a banner that shows for legal cover while every pixel fires anyway. Defaults to US state privacy law: CCPA and CPRA for California plus Virginia, Colorado and other state laws, with an opt-out link and a do-not-sell-or-share signal. Folds in GDPR opt-in consent for EU visitors and India's DPDP Act consent rules for Indian visitors on the same store, each a market option that reads null unless the brand sells into that region.
encompasses: inventory every tracking pixel, tag and script currently firing on first page load
route each one behind a consent-management layer keyed to visitor region and explicit choice
confirm a rejected-consent or opted-out visitor genuinely does not fire the gated scripts, by checking network requests, not just the banner's own claim

set the correct default per region: an opt-out 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link for US state laws, opt-in for GDPR (EU market option), and opt-in for DPDP (India market option, reads null for US) rather than one global default
keep essential, non-tracking scripts (cart, checkout, payment) ungated so consent choices never break core function
log consent choices in a way the brand can produce as proof if ever asked
trigger: store setup for a US brand, or an EU- or India-facing brand, or a compliance audit finding

name: Build a restock waitlist and pre-launch password-page capture flow
what: Adds a notify-me capture on an out-of-stock PDP and a password-protected coming-soon page for a pre-launch or a limited drop, each wired to collect an email or an SMS number (with TCPA consent) by default, or a WhatsApp number in a WhatsApp-commerce market (India, EU, LATAM), and fire an automatic notification the moment stock or launch goes live, instead of losing that demand silently.
encompasses: add a notify-me form on any out-of-stock PDP, capturing email or an SMS number (with TCPA consent) by default, or a WhatsApp number in a market where that channel is in use
fire an automatic notification the moment the SKU is back in stock, ranked by signup order for a limited restock
build a password-protected coming-soon page for pre-launch or a drop, keeping it out of search indexes
capture waitlist signups into the brand's own list, never a third party's, so it feeds lifecycle directly
report waitlist size and back-in-stock conversion rate per SKU to size real demand before a reorder decision
inputs: email, SMS or WhatsApp capture tool
trigger: a top SKU goes out of stock, or a pre-launch or drop is planned

name: Watch competitor pricing and refresh truthful anchor-price copy on the PDP
what: A capability no tool sells yet in this exact form: reads the same publicly listed competitor prices used for reference elsewhere in the system on a schedule, and when the brand's own PDP carries an anchor-price comparison claim, checks it is still true and flags it for a copy refresh the moment a competitor's public price moves, so a comparison claim never goes stale or false, without ever copying competitor text, images or branding onto the page.
encompasses: read only publicly listed competitor prices already treated as signal elsewhere in the system, never scraped account data
match each PDP anchor-price or comparison claim to the specific competitor price it cites
flag a claim as stale the moment the cited competitor price changes enough to make the comparison inaccurate
propose the corrected comparison number for a human to approve before the copy changes
never let a comparison claim ship without a current, dated source behind it
keep this entirely separate from the brand's own private cost and margin data
trigger: a competitor price change is detected, or a scheduled weekly check

name: Audit and govern the app and script stack (extension: runtime JS conflict detection)
what: Extends the app and script audit beyond relevance and duplication to catch runtime conflicts: two installed apps writing to the same DOM element, a console error thrown only when two specific apps load together, or a script that silently stops firing after another app updates.
encompasses: crawl key page types with every app active and log console errors, not just app relevance
isolate which pair of apps causes a conflict by disabling one at a time in staging
detect two apps competing for the same DOM insertion point (both trying to own the cart drawer, for example)
flag a previously working script that has gone silent after an unrelated app update
outputs: conflict list with the two apps named
console error log per page type
trigger: a bug appears with no clear single cause after a new app install

name: Monitor post-launch store hygiene (extension: session-replay bug detection)
what: Extends the scheduled hygiene sweep with a continuous feed from the site's own session-replay tool, turning rage-clicks, dead-clicks and JS-error events into ranked bug tickets automatically instead of waiting for a support ticket to surface the same bug.
encompasses: pull rage-click, dead-click and JS-error events from the session-replay tool on a schedule
cluster repeated events by the same element and page into one ticket, not one per session
rank tickets by number of sessions affected, not by when they were reported
hand a ranked, evidenced bug list to the QA regression suite instead of a vague complaint
trigger: scheduled hygiene sweep, or a spike in a specific rage-click event

name: Run automated speed regression monitoring (extension: real-user Core Web Vitals)
what: Extends the lab-based synthetic speed budget check with a monthly pull of real-user Core Web Vitals (CrUX) from the PageSpeed Insights API and Search Console per template, catching field-data regressions a synthetic lab test on one connection profile can miss.
encompasses: pull CrUX field data per template (home, PDP, collection, checkout) monthly
compare field data pass/fail against the lab-based synthetic result for the same template
flag a template that fails in the field but passes in the lab as a real-device or real-network issue, not a false alarm
keep field data separate from lab data in the report so the two are never averaged together
inputs: Search Console Core Web Vitals report
trigger: monthly schedule

name: Optimize on-site search (extension: conversational search and self-learning merchandising)
what: Extends predictive-text, synonym-matched search with a conversational product-finder for natural-language queries, a self-learning synonym dictionary that adapts from real search-to-purchase behavior, and no-code merchandising rule scheduling the merchandiser can run without an engineering ticket.
encompasses: add a conversational search box that answers a natural-language query ('a gift under 2000 for a first anniversary') with real matching SKUs, not a canned response
let the synonym dictionary self-adjust from real query-to-purchase pairs, with a human review before a new synonym goes live
auto-propose a synonym or filter fix the moment a real query returns zero results or a low click-through, for founder approval before publishing
let merchandising rules (pin a product, schedule a promotion, boost a season) be scheduled and published without an engineering ticket
watch for and correct search results still surfacing an out-of-stock or discontinued SKU
trigger: search-term audit finds recurring zero-result or low-CTR queries

name: Design on-site personalization (extension: page-level personalization by segment without engineering)
what: Extends quiz-driven and real-time-signal personalization with page-level variants of a homepage or landing page served by traffic source, geography, device or campaign UTM, using the page-builder's native personalization rules rather than a custom engineering build for every variant.
encompasses: define page variants keyed to a real segment (paid-search visitor vs organic, mobile vs desktop, a specific ad campaign's UTM)
build each variant inside the page-builder's native personalization feature instead of a bespoke script per variant
cap the number of live variants to what the traffic can actually prove out, avoiding a variant with too little volume to ever read
report which variant each segment saw alongside its conversion, so a variant is never judged on vanity traffic alone
trigger: a bottleneck is diagnosed as message-match, not raw traffic

name: Audit and remediate site accessibility (extension: reject overlay-only fixes, add continuous CI scan)
what: Extends the manual and automated WCAG audit with an explicit rule against relying on an accessibility overlay widget (accessiBe, UserWay-style) as the fix, since automated overlays catch only a fraction of real issues and one such vendor was fined for overstating what its widget could do, and adds a continuous automated accessibility scan tied into the CI pipeline so a new deploy cannot silently reintroduce a fixed issue.
encompasses: flag an overlay widget already installed as cosmetic cover, not a fix, and recommend manual remediation of the underlying markup instead
run an automated accessibility scanner on every CI deploy, not only at audit time
block a deploy that reintroduces a previously fixed contrast, alt-text or keyboard-trap issue
keep the manual keyboard and screen-reader test on the launch cadence, since automated scans catch roughly a third to two-fifths of real issues on their own
trigger: an overlay widget is found installed, or the CI pipeline is being set up

name: Implement structured data and schema markup (extension: continuous drift monitoring)
what: Extends the one-time structured-data build with continuous drift monitoring: re-validating Product, Offer, Review, BreadcrumbList and FAQPage markup against a rich-results validator after every theme deploy, since a theme or app update can silently strip or break JSON-LD without any visible page change.
encompasses: run every page type's structured data through a rich-results validator after each deploy, not only at initial build
diff the current JSON-LD against the last known-good version per template to catch silent stripping
alert when a theme or app update removes or malforms a schema block
track rich-result impression trends as a leading indicator that markup is still being read correctly
trigger: every theme or app deploy, tied into the CI pipeline

name: Configure payment gateways and go-live test (extension: scheduled recurring real test purchase)
what: Extends the one-time go-live payment test with a scheduled recurring real test purchase on production, using a small refundable amount, so a later settings, tax or shipping-rate change that breaks the payment path is caught within a day instead of by the next real customer complaint.
encompasses: run a real, small, refundable test purchase through production on a schedule, not only once at launch
cover the primary and a secondary payment method in rotation across scheduled runs
auto-refund the test purchase immediately and log the refund so it never shows as real revenue
alert immediately if a scheduled test purchase fails at any step, before a real customer hits the same failure
re-run the test automatically after any change to tax, shipping or payment settings, not only on the fixed schedule
trigger: scheduled interval, or any tax, shipping or payment settings change

name: Configure tax by jurisdiction (extension: sales tax nexus, automation and India GST invoicing)
what: Extends jurisdiction tax configuration with US sales tax nexus tracking and automation: registers economic nexus by state, applies marketplace facilitator rules so tax is not double-collected, connects Avalara or TaxJar for real-time rate calculation and filing, collects resale certificates from wholesale buyers, and produces 1099-K reporting. Where the brand also sells in India, adds the market option of GSTIN-compliant invoicing (an HSN code held per SKU, and the CGST/SGST versus IGST split computed from the buyer's state against the seller's registered state); this option reads null for US.
encompasses: track economic nexus by state from the brand's own sales volume and transaction count, and flag a new state that crosses the threshold
apply marketplace facilitator rules so tax a marketplace already collected is not double-charged on the brand's own site
connect Avalara or TaxJar for real-time rate calculation and automated filing across nexus states
collect and keep a resale certificate on file per wholesale buyer before exempting them from sales tax
produce 1099-K reporting against the brand's own payment processor threshold
India market option, reads null for US: hold an HSN code per SKU in the product record, not just a tax class
India market option, reads null for US: compute CGST plus SGST for an intra-state order and IGST for an inter-state order, in code from the buyer and seller state
India market option, reads null for US: generate a GSTIN-compliant invoice PDF per order via an invoicing app or native flow
India market option, reads null for US: flag a SKU missing its HSN code before it can be sold, rather than shipping an invoice with a blank field
inputs: India market option, null for US: seller GSTIN and state
India market option, null for US: per-SKU HSN code
India market option, null for US: buyer's billing state
outputs: India market option, null for US: GST invoice PDF per order
